docs.occupied.component: `Occupied` is what becomes of the one ALREADY in the slot when a drop lands on it —
`reject`, `merge`, `swap`, or `capture{to}`. This is NOT the `Acceptor`'s job: the rule
answers "may this one enter" and is silent about the sitter. Mixing the two was a smell of
an earlier client — the rule that lets a piece in should not also decide the fate of the
The outcome is DATA describing what moves, carried by `Displacer` on the container:
import { node, Container, Acceptor, Displacer, capture,
installStockOccupied(); // reject · swap · merge, under their own names
A container without a `Displacer` never clobbers a sitter: the conservative default is
`reject`, whether the container carries the atom at all or names a policy nobody registered.
docs.occupied.cell: One cell, one sitter, and a spare piece to drop on it. Pick the policy: `reject` bounces the
incomer home, `merge` leaves both standing in the cell, `capture` sends the sitter to the
tray beside it and the incomer takes the slot. `swap` reads correctly in the registry but has
no picture on this shelf — nothing here carries it out yet.
